method: Rungs 1-4 and 6-8 worked without a figure; zero searches used. ROUTE: econometricsociety.org/regions/world-congress links the calendar entry for the 2025 Seoul congress, and that page's only programme link is the Oxford Abstracts app. NEW FINDING worth carrying forward: Oxford Abstracts exposes an UNAUTHENTICATED Hasura GraphQL endpoint at https://graphql.oxfordabstracts.com/v1/graphql (named in https://virtual.oxfordabstracts.com/config.js as HASURA_URL). It answers introspection and real queries — {events(where:{event_title:{_ilike:"%conometric%"}}){id event_title event_start_date}} returns four Econometric Society regional meetings with their ids — BUT the public schema exposes only 12 query fields, all registration-related (events, events_by_pk, dr_tickets, dr_order_data, dr_invoice_setup ...); there is NO submissions or programme table, and the 2025 World Congress is not among the events it returns. So the API cannot count this congress; it is still worth recording as a route for other Oxford Abstracts meetings. NEEDS_RUNG_5, exact page: https://virtual.oxfordabstracts.com/#/e/eswc2025/program — open it in a browser and enumerate the programme, counting PAPERS inside sessions and excluding the separately listed invited lectures, presidential address and plenaries.

conference: NSTA National Conference on Science Education
abstracts: UNKNOWN — no session count and no sourced attendance figure; the session browser is a Blazor Server app
cadence_evidence: The National Conference runs annually (Philadelphia 26-29 March 2025, Indianapolis 4-7 November 2026, both on nsta.org). NOTE for the orchestrator: the field notes warn that NSTA runs several event families in parallel (national, area/spring conferences, joint meetings); only the National Conference is this row.
character_evidence: Decisive and taken from the organiser's own words, not assumed. NSTA's published Session Types are: Poster Sessions ('describe strategies or tools ... in a share-a-thon format'), Speed Sharing (10-15 minutes, three presenters an hour), Exhibitor Workshops (vendor-hosted product sessions), 30-minute Presentation ('share innovative teaching ideas, present research findings, or discuss a topic of general or specific interest'), 30-minute Roundtable (moderated discussion), 60-minute Presentation, 60-minute Workshop ('audience participation from a student's perspective') and 120-minute Professional Learning Workshop. Research reporting is ONE option inside one format. The exhibitor invitation sells 'the nation's largest audience of science teachers and administrators - key purchasers of education products', with 'over 90% of attendees directly purchase or influence purchases'. That is the NCTM pattern in the field notes, not the DGPs pattern.
programme_type: Blazor Server session browser on portal.nsta.org, plus a one-page schedule-at-a-glance PDF
programme_evidence: https://portal.nsta.org/conference/sessions returns a 7,895-byte Blazor Server shell (the markup contains a Blazor prerender descriptor and nothing else) — the data arrives over SignalR, so curl and WebFetch see no sessions. The linked schedule PDF (NSTA_NationalConf_INDY26_schedule_8626.pdf, HTTP 200, 218,277 bytes) is ONE page, a schedule at a glance with no session list. The 2025 GoEshow host s6.goeshow.com/nsta/national/2025/philadelphia/ is the EXHIBITOR portal only: it carries booth rates and an invitation to exhibit, and its session_search.cfm / full_session_search.cfm paths 404.
method: Rungs 1-8 worked without a figure, and rung 9 could NOT be run honestly: one search plus the society's own exhibits page, media rate card and exhibitor invitation produced NO attendance number at all — only 'thousands of attendees' and 'the largest science education association's show in the world'. The rate card (NSTARateCardsNSTAReports2026.pdf) carries only the NSTA Reports circulation of 200,000, which is a newspaper readership and NOT a conference headcount; it is recorded here purely so nobody mistakes it for one later. SNIPPET REJECTED: the phase-1 note's 'over 1,400 presentations and workshops' appears nowhere on https://www.nsta.org/national-conference-science-education-indianapolis-2026 or on the Sessions and Workshops page — both were opened in full and neither states any number — so it is not recorded. NEEDS_RUNG_5, exact pages: (1) https://portal.nsta.org/conference/sessions — open in a browser, browse all sessions and count them by type; (2) if a headcount is wanted for a rung-9 fallback, the NSTA exhibitor prospectus PDF (not linked from https://www.nsta.org/exhibits, which shows only booth rates) or a post-conference press release. COUNTING RULE when the browser opens it: per the NCTM precedent a 30-, 60- or 120-minute practitioner workshop yields about ONE presentation, and Exhibitor Workshops must be excluded outright as vendor sessions. Searched in English.

cadence_evidence: Annual: ala.org/annual redirects to 2027.alaannual.org while 2026.alaannual.org serves the current conference (Chicago, McCormick Place, 27-28 June 2026 poster days) — one edition site per year
character: practitioner, with ONE clearly bounded contributed-research track
character_evidence: The character question the queue asks is answerable from ALA's own words, and the answer is narrow. ALA describes Poster Sessions as 'a key professional development and engagement opportunity ... six categories of posters highlighting innovative library programs, research on emergent issues, and strategic initiatives', run as 90-minute drop-in sessions. The six categories are Outreach and Engagement, The Educators, Diversity Fair, Global Perspectives & Approaches, Infrastructure and The Collectors, each co-sponsored by an ALA division or office. Everything else in the programme is professional development, featured speakers, a film programme, an exhibits marketplace and division business — there is no open call for contributed papers anywhere on the conference site.
programme_type: eventScribe conference scheduler, with a poster-filtered agenda view
programme_evidence: https://annual2026.eventscribe.net/agenda.asp?BCFO=PO&pfp=Posters&all=1 returns the Cloudflare 'Attention Required' interstitial, HTTP 403, 5,511 bytes — the field notes' note that eventScribe defeats curl but not a browser applies exactly
method: Rungs 1-4 and 6-8 worked without a figure; zero searches used. ROUTE: www.ala.org/conferencesevents leads to the per-year site 2026.alaannual.org, whose Programming menu separates 'Poster Sessions' from every other programme element. The poster page itself links the ONE agenda view that is the contributed set: eventScribe filtered to posters. NEEDS_RUNG_5, exact page: https://annual2026.eventscribe.net/agenda.asp?BCFO=PO&pfp=Posters&fa=&fb=&fc=&fd=&all=1 — open in a browser (the all=1 parameter already asks for the unpaginated list) and count the poster entries; the six categories on the poster page give a per-category cross-check. COUNT ONLY THE POSTERS: ALA's conference programme is professional development, not contributed research, so the session list at https://annual2026.eventscribe.net/ must NOT be counted as abstracts. If the poster count comes in far below the bar, that IS positive evidence for this row, because the poster programme is the whole of ALA's contributed research — unlike a partial artefact, nothing is hidden behind it.
